title.narrative: Integrated WASH, Health, and Nutrition for Vulnerable and Underserved Communities in Aleppo and Al-Hasakeh

description.narrative: ltpgtThe proposed 12-month intervention aims to address critical and essential needs by increasing access to, and quality of, WASH and health services while improving nutrition outcomes for vulnerable communities in targeted sub-districts of Aleppo and Al-Hasakeh governorates. Action Against Hunger (ACF) will utilise a multi-sectoral and integrated approach to deliver impactful activities across WASH, Health, and Nutrition to underserved areas to reach over 205,000 people. The approach is founded on a robust needs assessment which involves a variety of stakeholders from the community to a national level and utilises tried and tested activities developed through the delivery of previous and existing programmes. What’s more, the action aims to promote the centrality of protection by reducing and preventing the exposure of adults and children to risks, and gender equality by considering the specific needs and constraints faced by women, girls, boys, and men, at all stages of the project cycle.lt/pgtltpgtltbrgtSpecifically, ACF will improve access to safe water through humanitarian emergency response for water crisis-affected populations by providing lifesaving daily water trucking to 72,000 individuals in Al-Hasakeh City for 5 months, utilising 24 trucks a day to reach a target of 1,000m3 per day. Simultaneously, ACF will conduct emergency light maintenance of water systems in the Al-Hasakeh governorate based on requests from targeted sub-districts: Al-Hasakeh, Derbasiyeh, Quamishli, and Qahtaniyyeh. These areas are suffering from a severe water crisis, and the project aims to alleviate hardships by responding to urgent requests and ensuring existing water systems are fully functioning. This includes repairs to broken systems, such as submersible pump units and well pipelines, impacting 7,000 beneficiaries. The locations for light rehabilitations will be selected based on emergency alerts raised by local stakeholders, including the Directorate of Water Resources (DoWR) and UNICEF. The action will enhance sanitation infrastructure and access for underserved people through the repair, reconstruction and operational support of the sanitation system in Tal Hasel. This will address critical issues with Tal Hasel's sewage system, which has fallen into severe disrepair, and prevent the transmission of waterborne diseases.lt/pgtltpgtltbrgtIn addition, ACF will increase access to and availability of health care services for over 30,000 people in vulnerable communities in As-Safira sub-district in Aleppo. ACF will build on organisational experience and the active community health program (delivered and funded through other projects) in As-Safira to enhance referral pathways and strengthen links to public health facilities as Tal Hasel PHC will undergo light rehabilitation. In addition, the action will strengthen the capacity of 20 healthcare workers (CHWs) from As-Safira health district, including Tal Hasel PHC, related to health service provision, integrated management of child illnesses, infectious diseases, and mental health.lt/pgtltpgtltbrgtComplementing Health activities, ACF will improve malnutrition monitoring, case detection, and facility reporting through nutrition surveillance and CMAM programmes in two PHCs in As-Safira and Al-Hasakeh. This integrates nutrition into the health system, while directly responding to the challenge of severe under-reporting related to nutrition programs at the governorate and national level. Inaccurate reporting continues to hinder effective decision-making related to Community-Based Management of Acute Malnutrition (CMAM) and Infant and young child feeding (IYCF) programming, contributes to the low identification and admission rate for malnutrition cases.ltbrgtlt/pgt
